options: B) The Earth's structure, composition, and history
questions.correct_answer: B) The Earth's structure, composition, and history
questions.explanation: Geology studies the Earth's PHYSICAL structure (rocks, minerals), COMPOSITION (what it's made of), and HISTORY (how it changed over time). Weather/climate is Meteorology, population is Human Geography, political boundaries is Political Geography.

ENDOGENIC (internal) forces come from INSIDE the Earth — from the mantle and core. They include folding, faulting, volcanism, and uplift. These forces BUILD UP the Earth's surface, creating mountains and plateaus.

VOLCANISM is an ENDOGENIC (internal) force — it comes from magma INSIDE the Earth. Weathering (A), water erosion (B), and wind erosion (D) are all EXOGENIC (external) forces that wear down the surface.

questions.text: Examine the diagram. What does the GREEN box represent?

questions.explanation: The GREEN box (left) contains Folding, Faulting, and Volcanism — these are ENDOGENIC (internal) forces. The RED box (right) with Weathering and Erosion is EXOGENIC (external).

questions.text: The Great Rift Valley in Ethiopia was formed by which ENDOGENIC process?
questions.explanation: The Great Rift Valley was formed by FAULTING — the breaking and downward movement of rock blocks due to tectonic forces. This is an ENDOGENIC process. Wind erosion, glaciation, and river deposition are EXOGENIC.

questions.text: The Earth is approximately how old?
questions.explanation: The Earth formed approximately 4.6 BILLION years ago. This vast time is divided into Eons, Eras, Periods, and Epochs. Human civilization is only about 10,000 years old — a tiny fraction of geological time.

questions.text: Examine the time scale. Which is the OLDEST era?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='180' viewBox='0 0 350 180'><rect width='350' height='180' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><rect x='20' y='30' width='310' height='25' rx='4' fill='#1a2332' stroke='#6d28d9' stroke-width='2'/><text x='175' y='48' text-anchor='middle' fill='#6d28d9' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>PRECAMBRIAN</text><rect x='20' y='65' width='310' height='25' rx='4' fill='#1a2332' stroke='#14b8a6' stroke-width='2'/><text x='175' y='83' text-anchor='middle' fill='#14b8a6' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>PALEOZOIC</text><rect x='20' y='100' width='310' height='25' rx='4' fill='#1a2332' stroke='#f59e0b' stroke-width='2'/><text x='175' y='118' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f59e0b' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>MESOZOIC</text><rect x='20' y='135' width='310' height='25' rx='4' fill='#1a2332' stroke='#f43f5e' stroke-width='2'/><text x='175' y='153' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f43f5e' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>CENOZOIC</text></svg>
questions.explanation: PRECAMBRIAN (purple, top) is the OLDEST era (4.6 billion to 541 million years ago). The order from oldest to youngest: Precambrian → Paleozoic → Mesozoic → Cenozoic. Superposition principle: oldest at bottom, but in this diagram the oldest is shown at TOP for simplicity.

options: A) Gives exact age in years
B) Determines which rocks are OLDER or YOUNGER (no exact age)
D) Only works on living things
questions.correct_answer: B) Determines which rocks are OLDER or YOUNGER (no exact age)
questions.explanation: RELATIVE dating only tells you the ORDER of events (which is older/younger) WITHOUT giving an exact age. ABSOLUTE dating gives the EXACT age in years. Carbon-14 and uranium dating are ABSOLUTE methods.

options: A) Rocks billions of years old
B) Organic materials up to ~50,000 years old
questions.correct_answer: B) Organic materials up to ~50,000 years old
questions.explanation: Carbon-14 dating works on ORGANIC materials (once-living things) up to about 50,000 years old. For older rocks (millions/billions of years), geologists use Uranium-238, Potassium-Argon, or Rubidium-Strontium dating.

options: A) Older rocks are on TOP of younger rocks
B) Older rocks are at BOTTOM, younger on TOP
C) All rocks are the same age
questions.correct_answer: B) Older rocks are at BOTTOM, younger on TOP
questions.explanation: SUPERPOSITION: In undisturbed rock layers, the OLDEST rocks are at the BOTTOM and the YOUNGEST are at the TOP. This is because new sediments are deposited ON TOP of older ones. This is a key principle of RELATIVE dating.
